segments.text: Welcome to the hockey season!
In this video, we will show you how to dress a youth goaltender.
To get started, you will need the following equipment.
Before you leave the house, make sure you have every piece of equipment.
To help with this, place your gear in the bag in the order you put it on.
This helps ensure all your gear will make it to and from the rink.
You will first start with your base layer of clothing.
Use something that's comfortable and breathable.
Pull on your hockey pants and make sure to tighten them accordingly.
Then put on your knee pads.
Pull your hockey socks over the knee pads and attach them to a garter belt.
Next, you will put on your hockey skates.
Make sure there are no laces that are dragging on the ice or being stepped on.
You will then attach the goalie pads to your skates.
This can be tricky for young goalies and is best if the parents help.
Lay the pad out in front of your skate.
Then tie your skate as seen in the video to get at least one inch of skate lace between your skate and the pad.
This is essential so your skate can rotate in your pads while skating and while in your butterfly.
You will then loop through the first hole of the skate, then the middle, and then through the back.
Bring the skate lace over the top and tie a bow.
Start attaching straps and work from the bottom up.
The bottom strap should feed through under the back part of your skate.
This strap should also remain fairly loose to allow the pad to rotate.
Then attach the rest of the straps and make sure the ones at the top of the pad near the knee are loose.
This helps goalies width and balance in their butterfly position.
Then goalies should put on their neck and chest protector.
Chest protectors can be tucked into the pants or can hang over the pants, whatever is comfortable.
Also remember to tighten your belt but not too tight as we want to maximize coverage area.
If a goalie wears suspenders, they should be pulled over the chest protector in this step.
Make sure to put on your jersey before putting on your gloves.
Now it's time to put on your helmet and gloves.
Gloves can be tightened with the velcro straps inside.
Last but not least, grab your stick and go play hockey.
